questions.prompt: The numbers of books read by 5 students during a holiday are 4, 6, 6, 8, and 11.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the mean number of books read, and state the median.

questions.prompt: A student records the scores of 5 tests: 21, 22, 24, 25, 73. The student observes that the score 73 is an extreme value.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State which measure of central tendency, the mean or the median, is more appropriate to represent a typical score, giving a reason.

questions.prompt:
An ordered stem-and-leaf diagram displays the ages of 9 people. The stem represents tens and the leaf represents units:
$$\begin{array}{r|l} 1 & 8 \\ 2 & 1\quad 4\quad 4\quad 7 \\ 3 & 0\quad 2\quad 5 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down a suitable key for this diagram, and find the median age.

questions.prompt: A researcher wishes to display a dataset of 50 exam scores. State one advantage of using a stem-and-leaf diagram rather than a box-and-whisker plot.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State one advantage of a stem-and-leaf diagram over a box-and-whisker plot.

questions.prompt: A grouped frequency table gives the lengths of 20 metal rods in cm: 5 rods in the interval $10 \le x < 12$ and 15 rods in the interval $12 \le x < 16$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequency density of each class interval.

questions.prompt:
Two groups of runner times have the following five-number summaries in minutes:
Group X: Minimum $= 20$, $Q_1 = 25$, Median $= 28$, $Q_3 = 34$, Maximum $= 42$.
Group Y: Minimum $= 18$, $Q_1 = 22$, Median $= 31$, $Q_3 = 36$, Maximum $= 45$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Compare the typical running time and the spread of the middle 50% of times for Group X and Group Y.

questions.prompt: Twelve athletes were asked to record the time, in seconds, taken to complete an agility drill. Their times are: 14, 15, 15, 16, 17, 18, 18, 19, 20, 22, 24, 45.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the median and the interquartile range of the agility drill times.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Give a disadvantage of using the mean as a measure of central tendency for these times, identifying the relevant feature of the data.

questions.prompt:
The table below shows the distribution of scores achieved by 40 students in a mathematics contest:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Score interval} & 10 - 19 & 20 - 29 & 30 - 39 & 40 - 49 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 6 & 14 & 12 & 8 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the modal class, and identify the class interval that contains the median.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate an estimate of the mean score of the 40 students.

questions.prompt:
The stem-and-leaf diagram below shows the test percentages scored by 15 students in Physics:
$$\begin{array}{r|lllll} 4 & 2 & 5 & 8 & & \\ 5 & 1 & 4 & 6 & 7 & 9 \\ 6 & 0 & 3 & 5 & 8 & \\ 7 & 2 & 6 & & & \end{array}$$
Key: $5 \mid 1 = 51\%$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the median test score and the interquartile range.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: An outlier is defined as any value that lies more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ below $Q_1$ or above $Q_3$. Determine whether there are any outliers in this dataset.

questions.prompt:
A continuous variable $X$ represents the weights in grams of 50 samples, grouped into classes:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Weight } (x\text{ g}) & 20 \le x < 30 & 30 \le x < 35 & 35 \le x < 45 & 45 \le x < 60 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 12 & 15 & 13 & 10 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequency density of each class interval for a histogram.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On a histogram representing this data, the bar for the class $30 \le x < 35$ has a width of $2\text{ cm}$ and a height of $9\text{ cm}$. Find the width and height of the bar for the class $45 \le x < 60$.

questions.prompt:
Two car rental companies, Alpha and Beta, track the daily mileage of their customer rentals. The five-number summaries in miles are:
Alpha: Minimum $= 40$, $Q_1 = 65$, Median $= 85$, $Q_3 = 110$, Maximum $= 160$.
Beta: Minimum $= 50$, $Q_1 = 80$, Median $= 95$, $Q_3 = 115$, Maximum $= 155$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Compare the typical daily mileage and overall spread between Alpha and Beta.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Compare the spread of the middle 50% of the mileage for both companies, and state one advantage of using paired box-and-whisker plots on the same scale for this comparison.

questions.prompt:
The masses, in kg, of 11 members of a rowing crew and 11 members of a rugby team are recorded as follows:
Rowers: 72, 75, 78, 80, 81, 82, 84, 85, 88, 91, 95.
Rugby: 68, 74, 76, 79, 82, 85, 87, 88, 90, 92, 115.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: For the rugby team, show that the mass $115\text{ kg}$ is an outlier using the criterion that outliers lie more than $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ above the upper quartile.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Construct an ordered back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram to represent the masses of the members of both teams, placing Rowers on the left and Rugby on the right.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the median and the interquartile range of the masses of the rowers. Hence compare the masses of the two teams, referring to both central tendency and spread.

questions.prompt:
The table below gives the distribution of the commute times, in minutes, for 85 employees of a company:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Commute time } (t\text{ min}) & 0 \le t < 20 & 20 \le t < 30 & 30 \le t < 45 & 45 \le t < 60 & 60 \le t < 80 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 10 & 15 & 30 & 18 & 12 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the frequency density for each class interval.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On a histogram representing this data, the bar for the class $20 \le t < 30$ has a width of $5\text{ cm}$ and a height of $6\text{ cm}$. Find the total area, in $\text{cm}^2$, of the bars representing the entire histogram.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate an estimate of the mean commute time, and identify the class interval containing the median commute time.
